mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Corporate registry of the jurisdiction of incorporation of the general partner (e.g., analogous state or provincial registry)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all UBOs, general partners, limited partners holding 25% or more, and authorized signatories against: (i) the United Nations Security Council Consolidated List; (ii) Global Affairs Canada consolidated sanctions list under the Special Economic Measures Act, United Nations Act, and the Justice for Victims of Corrupt Foreign Officials Act (Sergei Magnitsky Law); (iii) OFAC SDN and 13559 list where USD wire rails, US correspondent banks, or US persons are involved; (iv) FINTRAC guidance on politically exposed persons (PEPs) and heads of international organizations, including PEP family members and close associates; and (v) public registries of bankruptcy, director disqualification, and criminal records where legally permissible. Enhanced due diligence is mandatory for PEPs, FATF high-risk jurisdictions, unusual beneficial-ownership structures, and nominees. The retained law firm and financial intermediary will document the screening result in a written risk assessment; unresolved hits require disengagement and, where a reporting entity is involved, filing of a Suspicious Transaction Report with FINTRAC. Counsel performs the UBO piercing analysis under the BC Limited Partnership Act transparency-register rules, reaching through corporate, trust, and nominee layers until each individual with significant control is identified.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: BC Corporate Registry via BC Registries and Online Services (BC Corporate Online), operated by the Registrar of Companies; online portal: www.bconline.gov.bc.ca; alternative paper filings accepted by the Victoria office of BC Registries
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The limited partnership name must be expressed in English or French using Latin-script characters accepted by the BC registry; the statutory requirement for a BC limited partnership is that the name end with 'Limited Partnership', 'L.P.', or 'LP' (French equivalents permitted where applicable). Non-Latin scripts (e.g., Chinese, Cyrillic) must be transliterated into Latin script, and a certified transliteration may be required by the Registrar; punctuation, numbers, and standard symbols are permitted only in accordance with BC naming policy.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Name reservations are issued by the BC Registrar of Companies for 56 days under the standard BC Corporate Online name-request procedure and are not extendable; if the reservation period lapses before the limited partnership is registered, the applicant must file a new name request and pay the fee again. If the Registrar rejects a proposed name, the applicant may file a revised Name Request with the BC Corporate Registry or submit a written Request for Reconsideration to the Registrar of Companies within 30 days of the refusal, explaining compliance with the BC name provisions; reconsideration is a discretionary administrative review. Where the Registrar confirms the refusal, the applicant may seek judicial review in the Supreme Court of British Columbia under the Judicial Review Procedure Act, R.S.B.C. 1996, c. 241. Practical strategy includes obtaining a preliminary trade-mark clearance and requesting conditional approval where the first-choice name carries a 'similar' hit.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Conditionally permitted. The BC Limited Partnership Act requires the limited partnership to maintain a record office with a physical street address in British Columbia at which the records, including the transparency register, are kept and where process may be served during normal business hours. A reputable virtual-office or registered-agent service is acceptable only if it provides a physical BC street address, accepts service of process, maintains the required statutory records, and is not a mere post-office box or mail-forwarding service. For the stated medical-device manufacturing sector, a virtual-office arrangement without operational premises in BC will not satisfy commercial-substance expectations of banking partners or Health Canada for the future establishment licence, although it is legally sufficient for incorporation purposes.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low to Moderate (estimated 10% to 15% within the first 12 months). Unannounced physical premises inspections are uncommon for corporate-registry purposes; most Registrar and law-enforcement examinations occur desk-based at the record office under a 10-day production order. The risk increases if any UBO or general partner triggers a PEP, sanctions, or high-risk-jurisdiction flag, or if the BC Registrar or CRA launches an audit; CRA field visits may occur without advance notice in respect of source-of-funds and residency issues.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Partnership Act, R.S.B.C. 1996, c. 348, Part 3 (Limited Partnerships), particularly s. 55 (Registration of limited partnership) and ss. 51-64 General; Business Corporations Act, S.B.C. 2002, c. 57 (governing the corporate General Partner).
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: BC Registries and Online Services, Ministry of Finance, Province of British Columbia — Corporate Online portal.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Declaration of Limited Partnership (Form LP-1) filed under s. 55 of the Partnership Act.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital for a British Columbia limited partnership; capital is determined contractually in the Limited Partnership Agreement. No escrow or trust account is mandated by the Partnership Act.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: FIRST BOARD RESOLUTION — GENERAL PARTNER OF [CA_LP]. RESOLVED: (1) The General Partner hereby subscribes to its partnership interest in the Limited Partnership in accordance with the executed Limited Partnership Agreement dated [DATE]; (2) the registered and records office of the Limited Partnership shall be situated at [REGISTERED OFFICE], British Columbia; (3) the following persons are appointed officers: [NAME] - Chief Executive Officer, [NAME] - Chief Financial Officer, and [NAME] - Corporate Secretary, with authority to act severally; (4) the Chief Executive Officer and Corporate Secretary are authorized to file the Declaration of Limited Partnership, open banking accounts, and execute all regulatory filings; and (5) this resolution takes effect immediately.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: BC Registries and Online Services — Corporate Online (corporateonline.gov.bc.ca)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Conduct a NUANS-preferred name search through an accredited search house or via Corporate Online. Submit up to three proposed names on a Name Reservation Request (Form NR) electronically; the reservation is valid for 56 calendar days and may be renewed once.
required_dossiers: Letter of authorization from the intended General Partner
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If a name is refused for conflict or similarity, file a new reservation request with a written explanation of distinguishing elements, or submit a written submission to the Registrar for a discretionary decision.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Federal CRA Registration for Business Number and Tax Accounts
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) — Business Registration Online (BRO) window
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Register the limited partnership for a federal Business Number (BN) and, as applicable, GST/HST (RT) account, payroll (RP) account, and import/export (RM) account via CRA Business Registration Online or Form RC1. GST/HST registration is mandatory once taxable supplies exceed CAD 30,000 (approx. USD 22,000) per Excise Tax Act, s. 240. Retain the confirmation letter with the assigned BN.
required_dossiers: Completed Form RC1 or BRO online application
BC Certificate of Registration for the Limited Partnership
Limited Partnership Agreement extract showing partners' names and business address
Letter from the corporate General Partner appointing the applicant as authorized representative
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the BN application is delayed or rejected, call the CRA Business Window (1-800-959-5525) for manual creation of the account; correct legal-name mismatches between BC Registries and CRA records; request expedited processing through the CRA National Verification Centre.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Provincial Registrations — PST, Employer Account and WorkSafeBC Clearance
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: BC Ministry of Finance (Consumer Taxation Branch) and WorkSafeBC
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Register for PST collection through eTaxBC if the partnership makes taxable retail sales in BC (medical device sales to hospitals are generally exempt; confirm applicability). Register as an employer with WorkSafeBC to obtain an industry classification and account number before the first payroll date, and request a Clearance Letter for the manufacturing site.
required_dossiers: BC eTaxBC PST registration form (if applicable)
BC Certificate of Registration for the Limited Partnership
Occupational health and safety program outline
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If PST registration is applied in error, file a deregistration request through eTaxBC with a written explanation. If WorkSafeBC assigns an incorrect industry classification, file a Notice of Objection under the Workers Compensation Act within the statutory deadline.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Municipal Business Licence and Zoning Verification
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: City or District municipality of the plant location (e.g., City of Vancouver — Development, Buildings, and Licensing department)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Apply for a municipal business licence through the local electronic licensing portal. Submit the floor plan of the manufacturing facility and obtain a zoning confirmation certificate proving that the site is zoned for light manufacturing or medical-device production (M-1/M-2). Pay the municipal fee (typically CAD 100 to CAD 1,000 depending on class and size).
required_dossiers: BC Certificate of Registration for the Limited Partnership
Zoning certificate or planning department confirmation letter
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the zoning designation is incompatible, file a Development Variance Permit application followed by the municipal land-use appeal process; provide revised engineering documentation if the planning office requests further environmental or structural review.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Health Canada — Health Products and Food Branch (HPFB), Medical Devices Directorate; co-regulator: BC Ministry of Environment and Climate Change Strategy
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Medical Device Establishment Licence (MDEL) under the Medical Devices Regulations, SOR/98-282, of the Food and Drugs Act, for manufacturing and selling Class II-IV titanium orthopedic implant devices; facility registration under ISO 13485:2016 via the Canadian Medical Devices Conformity Assessment System (CMDCAS)

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: BC Environmental Assessment Office (EAO) and BC Ministry of Environment and Climate Change Strategy — Environmental Protection Division
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Registration/Screening tier: a full EIA report is not triggered for electron beam 3D additive manufacturing of titanium implants because the operation falls below the mandatory thresholds of the Environmental Assessment Act; however, the facility must register as an industrial operation under the Environmental Management Act and obtain a Waste Discharge Authorization if point-source air or wastewater emissions are generated.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Compliance thresholds: Federal Metal Finishing Effluent Guidelines (CEPA 1999) and BC Municipal Wastewater Regulation — total suspended solids below 15 mg/L, oil and grease below 15 mg/L, pH 6.0-9.0, and cadmium/lead below analytical detection limits; air emissions per BC Air Quality Objectives for PM2.5 (25 µg/m3 24-hour) and PM10 (50 µg/m3 24-hour); volatile organic compounds regulated under the federal Multi-Sector Air Pollutants Regulations, SOR/2016-151; argon atmosphere is inert, so no VOC offset credit is required; titanium powder handling must comply with WHMIS 2015 and CSA/ANSI metal-powder containment standards.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certification under the BC Fire Code (SBC 2004, c.31) issued by the local fire marshal; Technical Safety BC inspection and clearance for argon pressure vessels and electrical systems under the Safety Standards Act; structural load inspection by the municipal building official for the electron beam chamber; WorkSafeBC occupational health and safety clearance covering Part 5 (Chemical Agents and Biological Agents), Part 8 (Personal Protective Equipment), and WHMIS 2015 training, plus an approved first-aid program.

mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Transport document: Bill of Lading / Air Waybill
Inward Remittance Certificate / bank FX evidence (SWIFT MT103)

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of Canada (Banque du Canada) and Financial Transactions and Reports Analysis Centre of Canada (FINTRAC) for AML/ATF; no specialized foreign exchange administration exists in Canada.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The Canadian dollar is independently floated and fully convertible for both current and capital account transactions. Canada maintains no foreign exchange control law; cross-border payments are unrestricted. Profit remittance by a British Columbia Limited Partnership to foreign partners is free from exchange-control approval, but may attract non-resident withholding tax under Part XIII of the Income Tax Act (typically 25% treaty-reduced) and must be reported on Canadian T4/T5 or NR4 filings as applicable. There are no local reinvestment or conversion hurdles for export proceeds earned in foreign currency.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: No statutory surrender requirement exists. Exporters are not obliged to convert foreign currency receivables into Canadian dollars and face no mandatory holding period, repatriation timeline, or deposit ratio with a Canadian bank. Receipts may be retained in foreign currency accounts; however, any conversion for operational use is executed through arm's-length banking channels at prevailing market rates.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Royal Bank of Canada (RBC) – British Columbia Commercial Banking
Bank of Montreal (BMO) – BC Commercial Banking
Canadian Imperial Bank of Commerce (CIBC) – BC Commercial Banking
HSBC Canada (now integrated into RBC) – Former International Account Base
tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Not separately available; legacy migrations only

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Medium. Canada does not issue 'Electronic Money Institution' licences. Online-only cross-border payment companies must register as Money Services Businesses (MSB) with FINTRAC and hold provincial registrations in British Columbia under the Money Services Business Act. Such entities may handle treasury settlement and FX conversion, but they are not chartered banks and cannot provide regulated deposit-taking, cheques, or escrow services. Legal viability is conditional on FINTRAC MSB registration, a Canadian compliance officer, and, depending on transaction profile, registration as a foreign money services business; outright offshore EMIs without Canadian MSB status may not lawfully serve the entity in Canada.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Physical presence of all directors is generally not a blanket statutory mandate. Canadian banks accept remote identity verification through BC notaries, credit unions authorized under the British Columbia Financial Institutions Act, or FINTRAC-compliant identification systems. Nevertheless, most Tier-1 banks formally require an in-person interview for the general partner's senior officer or partner, particularly where a new client presents as a foreign-sourced manufacturer. A pragmatic blueprint is to arrange a one-time video-enabled KYC call plus certified copies of passports and proof of address, while being prepared for a brick-and-mortar branch visit if the bank flags beneficial ownership complexity. A BC-registered limited partnership with a Canadian-resident general partner will materially reduce physical appearance demands.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Complex ownership chain with non-resident limited partners holding indirect interests
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Notarized corporate registry extract; chain-of-title diagram; valid Certificate of Limited Partnership; formal partnership agreement with partner capital schedules; national identity documents and in-person/remote KYC verification for all beneficial owners at 25% or greater; signed source-of-funds questionnaire; independent legal opinion confirming the LP is not an investment fund and the business is active manufacturing.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-value inbound wire transfers for initial LP capital contributions from foreign jurisdictions
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Pro forma invoices or equipment purchase orders from EBM 3D printing vendors; final private placement memorandum or capital subscription agreement; bank statement showing funds originated from an explained and legitimate liquidation event; tax clearance or proof of tax residence; transaction purpose codes and legally sufficient SWIFT reference letters from the remitting bank.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Sanctions or politically exposed person (PEP) name match in shareholder list or counterparty base
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: PEP clearance report from a reputable commercial screening service; negative news search results; explanation memorandum from the relevant partner; corporate due diligence forming part of a sanctions compliance policy; legal representation letters confirming no sanctioned country nexus; documented review by the BC branch AML officer.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-risk importer/exporter jurisdiction identified on trade finance documentary checks
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: End-user certificate for titanium orthopedic implants; purchase orders and airway bills tied to named hospitals or distributors; regulatory import approvals from Health Canada or the destination-country equivalent; product classification certificate under HS 9021; insurance certificates for shipments; independent third-party confirmation from FINTRAC-audited freight forwarder.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Compliant wire transfers must be denominated in Canadian dollars or freely convertible foreign currency and routed through a Canadian chartered bank account of the LP. Remitting banks must include accurate originator and beneficiary identifiers, the LP's full legal name, and a purpose code reflecting equity capital contribution. Internationally, SWIFT MT103 messages should carry a beneficiary account in Canada and a clear remittance information line such as 'Capital Contribution – Limited Partner 1 – Project Titanium Implant'. FINTRAC does not prescribe a binding purpose-code dictionary for capital injections; however, the bank's transaction review unit will require supporting documents demonstrating the capital contribution is not criminal proceeds. For cross-border flows exceeding C$10,000, the bank submits a Large Cash Transaction Report or EFT report to FINTRAC as applicable. Internal procedures must match remitter name to registered limited partner list and reconcile the wire with a dated partner capital account statement.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound trade settlements for EBM titanium implant manufacturing and export may use (i) SWIFT MT103 wire transfers for advance payments, open-account settlements, or pre-shipment deposit transfers; (ii) commercial documentary letters of credit (irrevocable, confirmed or unconfirmed) issued by the buyer's bank and advised/negotiated by the Canadian bank; and (iii) documentary collections with SI/DA terms. The LP must appoint the BC commercial bank as the receiving/negotiating bank for import LCs covering the electron-beam melting equipment, titanium powder feedstock, and ancillary consumables. Manually initiated MT103 outbound payments require completeness of beneficiary bank BIC, account/IBAN, and remittance references. Trade disbursements above CDN $100,000 may be routed via Canada's Large Value Transfer System (LVTS) or via SWIFT's international rails, with settlement in the Canadian bank's treasury desk. No Canadian exchange-control approval is required for export payments, but the underlying trade contract, invoices, packing lists, and applicable export permits under the Export Controls Handbook (including Health Canada medical device registration) must be retained.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Plain-vanilla foreign exchange forwards executed with a Canadian Schedule I chartered bank or an FINTRAC-registered treasury intermediary, covering USD/CAD and EUR/CAD receivables or payables on a delivery basis.
Cross-currency swaps (USD/CAD and EUR/CAD) used solely for transforming a foreign-currency debt or payment stream into Canadian dollars, with full documentation under an ISDA 2002 Master Agreement.
FX options as part of an annual hedging program with the bank's global markets desk, provided the instruments are not speculative and are fully covered by projected trade flows.

Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) are permissible when a hard-currency emerging-market trade receivable requires synthetic CAD hedging; however, given CAD full convertibility and deep onshore markets, NDFs are generally disfavoured and only used in counterparty-constrained corridors.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: British Columbia Registry and Information Services (Corporate Registry)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 60 days after each anniversary of the LP's registration date
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing fee of CAD 50; failure to file for two consecutive anniversary cycles triggers administrative strike-off and loss of limited liability shield.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Last day of the fifth month following the partnership fiscal year-end; for a calendar-year fiscal period, May 31
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure-to-file penalties under subsections 162(7) to (8.1) of the Income Tax Act; 5% of unpaid partnership tax plus 1% per month up to 12 months, plus any gross-negligence penalties.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: T4 Statement of Remuneration and T4 Summary (Employer Annual Return)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: On or before the last day of February following the calendar year in which remuneration was paid
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing penalty of 5% of understated remittance plus 1% per month up to 12 months; $25 per day per missing T4 slip, minimum $100 and maximum $2,500, plus possible criminal prosecution for repeated wilful failures.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: No mandatory statutory audit is imposed on a private, non-reporting-issuer BC limited partnership under the Partnership Act or federal corporate statutes. A compulsory audit becomes applicable only if the LP is a 'reporting issuer' under the BC Securities Act, an 'investment fund' engaging in investing with a minimum public holding, or if the partnership agreement, lender covenant, or an applicable regulator requires audited financial statements. A limited partner may also demand an independent audit under the Partnership Act's full and true information rights.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Canadian GAAP: IFRS (Part I, CPA Canada Handbook) is required if the LP is a reporting issuer or is ineligible for ASPE; otherwise the general partner may elect ASPE (Part II). For income-tax reporting, the partnership computes income under the Income Tax Act and reconciles from accounting net income.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: British Columbia does not require an annual UBO attestation for limited partnerships. However, any change to limited partner interests, capital contributions, or legal ownership of partnership interests must be reported by amending the Statement of Registration with the BC Corporate Registry within 15 days of the change. The limited partnership must maintain at its registered office a current register of limited partners containing each partner's name, address, contribution, and transfer history; annual confirmation is recommended as a governance control but is not a separate statutory filing.

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 15% small business rate (federal) / 38% general rate (federal); BC provincial rates 11% small business / 12% general (note: Limited Partnerships are pass-through entities with no corporate tax)
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Manufacturing and Processing Profits Deduction (MPPD) up to 100% deduction for qualifying Canadian manufacturing and processing income; Small Business Deduction for active business income under $500,000

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: T5013 Partnership Information Return filed electronically via CRA My Account or e-filing portal
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: 6 months after fiscal year-end (e.g. 30 June for 31 December fiscal year-end)

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Aggregate income of the partnership from all sources including manufacturing operations
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Allocate income to non-resident partners per partnership agreement; report allocable share on partner personal returns

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Deductions claimed including capital cost allowance and other business expenses
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident partners claim their allocated share of deductions per agreement

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net income after deductions allocated to partners
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident partners report share on personal tax returns; no corporate tax payable by LP

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing penalty $50 per day maximum $1,000; interest on late payments at prescribed rates; possible personal liability of general partners for unpaid taxes

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: N/A for Limited Partnerships (no corporate dividends declared); distributions generally not subject to withholding tax
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: Not applicable to LP distributions; for interest or royalties, submit Treaty Relief Certificate (TRC) to CRA to claim reduced treaty rate
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Royalties: 10% statutory rate, reduced to 0-10% under applicable DTAs; Interest: 10% statutory rate, reduced to 0-15% under applicable DTAs

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: CAD 50 million in related-party transactions triggering Master File and Local File requirements
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: No formal Economic Substance Regulations; however, general anti-avoidance rule (GAAR) and transfer pricing rules require demonstration of real business operations and economic substance in British Columbia

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Deliberate underreporting of partnership income or false statements on T5013
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Criminal penalties including fines up to $100,000 and imprisonment up to 2 years; civil penalties for gross negligence
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: General partners face personal liability for tax debts; possible criminal charges and disqualification from office

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell Company / Lack of Economic Substance
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Establishing LP without real business operations, employees or assets in British Columbia
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Penalties under Income Tax Act up to $10,000 per day; GAAR adjustments denying tax benefits
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and general partners personally liable for penalties and possible jail time for willful non-compliance

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failure to conduct proper due diligence on beneficial owners or suspicious transaction reporting
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Fines up to $500,000 or more; criminal charges under Proceeds of Crime Act
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Personal fines, imprisonment, and potential travel bans or asset freezes
